---
title: "Attitude_Plot_Construction"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# JOB QUALITY AND POLITICAL ATTITUDES
# Coefficient Plot of JQI Components
#
# Outcomes:
#   1. Redistribution
#   2. Getting ahead
#   3. Children's future
#   4. Political efficacy
#   5. Tax attitudes
#
# Model:
#   outcome ~ employment status + social class +
#             compensation + benefits + earnings stability
#
# Data:
#   GSS cumulative file, 2000-2024
#   Industry-year Job Quality Index merged by industry/year
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# 1. PACKAGES
# ============================================================

library(gssr)
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(broom)
library(here)


# ============================================================
# 2. LOAD FULL CUMULATIVE GSS DATA
# ============================================================

data(gss_all, package = "gssr")


# Restrict to analysis period
gss_years <- gss_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    as.numeric(year) >= 2000,
    as.numeric(year) <= 2024
  )


# ============================================================
# 3. VARIABLES NEEDED FOR THIS ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

# We only need the variables necessary for:
#   - industry/year merge
#   - employment status
#   - social class
#   - five political attitudes

gss_attitudes <- gss_years %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    id,
    indus10,
    wrkstat,
    class,
    eqwlth,
    getahead,
    kidssol,
    poleff11,
    tax
  )


# ============================================================
# 4. CONVERT INDUSTRY TO YOUR 14 COMMON INDUSTRIES
# ============================================================

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(indus10)
    ),
    
    industry_common = case_when(
      
      indus10_num == 770 ~
        "Construction",
      
      indus10_num >= 1070 &
        indus10_num <= 3990 ~
        "Manufacturing",
      
      indus10_num >= 4070 &
        indus10_num <= 4590 ~
        "Wholesale trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 4670 &
        indus10_num <= 5790 ~
        "Retail trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 6070 &
        indus10_num <= 6390 ~
        "Transportation and warehousing",
      
      indus10_num >= 6470 &
        indus10_num <= 6780 ~
        "Information",
      
      indus10_num >= 6870 &
        indus10_num <= 6990 ~
        "Finance and insurance",
      
      indus10_num >= 7070 &
        indus10_num <= 7190 ~
        "Real estate and rental and leasing",
      
      indus10_num >= 7270 &
        indus10_num <= 7490 ~
        "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7570 &
        indus10_num <= 7790 ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",
      
      indus10_num >= 7860 &
        indus10_num <= 7890 ~
        "Educational services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7970 &
        indus10_num <= 8470 ~
        "Health care and social assistance",
      
      indus10_num >= 8560 &
        indus10_num <= 8690 ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",
      
      indus10_num >= 8770 &
        indus10_num <= 9290 ~
        "Other services",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Load underlying job-quality measures
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_primary <- readRDS(
  here("01_tidydata", "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.rds")
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Construct the JQI components
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_for_gss <- job_quality_primary %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Compensation:
    # average of standardized CPS wage premium and
    # standardized ECEC wage cost per hour
    z_wage_premium = as.numeric(scale(wage_premium)),
    z_wage_cost = as.numeric(scale(wage_cost_per_hour)),
    
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_wage_cost
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Benefits:
    # non-required employer benefits
    z_benefits = as.numeric(scale(benefits_nonrequired)),
    
    benefits = z_benefits,
    
    # Earnings stability:
    # reverse the volatility measure so that higher values
    # indicate greater earnings stability
    z_earnings_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-earnings_volatility)
    ),
    
    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability,
    
    # Composite JQI
    jqi_primary = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    industry_common,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability,
    jqi_primary
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Merge JQI measures onto GSS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  left_join(
    job_quality_for_gss,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  )


# ============================================================
# 6. CREATE EMPLOYMENT STATUS VARIABLE
# ============================================================

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    wrkstat_factor = factor(
      as.numeric(wrkstat),
      levels = 1:8,
      labels = c(
        "Full-time",
        "Part-time",
        "Temporarily not working",
        "Unemployed",
        "Retired",
        "In school",
        "Keeping house",
        "Other"
      )
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 7. CREATE SOCIAL CLASS VARIABLE
# ============================================================

# GSS CLASS:
#   1 = Lower class
#   2 = Working class
#   3 = Middle class
#   4 = Upper class
#   5 = No class

# We exclude "no class," as in the previous analyses.

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    social_class_factor = case_when(
      
      as.numeric(class) == 1 ~
        "Lower class",
      
      as.numeric(class) == 2 ~
        "Working class",
      
      as.numeric(class) == 3 ~
        "Middle class",
      
      as.numeric(class) == 4 ~
        "Upper class",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    social_class_factor = factor(
      social_class_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 8. RECODE POLITICAL ATTITUDE OUTCOMES
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Redistribution
#
# EQWLTH:
# 1 = Government should reduce differences
# ...
# 7 = Differences do not need to be reduced
#
# Higher = less support for redistribution
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    redistribution = case_when(
      as.numeric(eqwlth) %in% 1:7 ~
        as.numeric(eqwlth),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Getting ahead
#
# 1 = Hard work
# 2 = Both hard work and luck
# 3 = Luck
#
# Higher = greater emphasis on luck
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    getting_ahead = case_when(
      as.numeric(getahead) %in% 1:3 ~
        as.numeric(getahead),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Children's future
#
# 1 = Much better
# 2 = Somewhat better
# 3 = About the same
# 4 = Somewhat worse
# 5 = Much worse
# 6 = No children
#
# Reverse so that higher = greater optimism
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    childrens_future = case_when(
      as.numeric(kidssol) %in% 1:5 ~
        6 - as.numeric(kidssol),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Political efficacy
#
# POLEFF11:
# 1 = Strongly agree that people like me have no say
# ...
# 5 = Strongly disagree
#
# Higher = greater political efficacy
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    political_efficacy = case_when(
      as.numeric(poleff11) %in% 1:5 ~
        as.numeric(poleff11),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Tax attitudes
#
# 1 = Taxes are too high
# 2 = About right
# 3 = Taxes are too low
# 4 = No income tax
#
# Drop 4.
# Higher = greater belief taxes are too low
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  mutate(
    
    tax_attitudes = case_when(
      as.numeric(tax) %in% 1:3 ~
        as.numeric(tax),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 9. CREATE MODEL DATASETS
# ============================================================

# We use the same independent variables in every model.
#
# This means each coefficient is estimated on the appropriate
# outcome-specific sample, rather than imposing unnecessary
# missingness across all five outcomes.

base_formula <- ~
  wrkstat_factor +
  social_class_factor +
  compensation +
  benefits +
  earnings_stability


# ============================================================
# 10. ESTIMATE ORDERED LOGIT MODELS
# ============================================================


attitude_models <- list(

  redistribution = MASS::polr(
    ordered(redistribution) ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = gss_attitudes %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(redistribution),
        !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
        !is.na(social_class_factor),
        !is.na(compensation),
        !is.na(benefits),
        !is.na(earnings_stability)
      ),
    Hess = TRUE
  ),

  getting_ahead = MASS::polr(
    ordered(getting_ahead) ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = gss_attitudes %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(getting_ahead),
        !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
        !is.na(social_class_factor),
        !is.na(compensation),
        !is.na(benefits),
        !is.na(earnings_stability)
      ),
    Hess = TRUE
  ),

  childrens_future = MASS::polr(
    ordered(childrens_future) ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = gss_attitudes %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(childrens_future),
        !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
        !is.na(social_class_factor),
        !is.na(compensation),
        !is.na(benefits),
        !is.na(earnings_stability)
      ),
    Hess = TRUE
  ),

  political_efficacy = MASS::polr(
    ordered(political_efficacy) ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = gss_attitudes %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(political_efficacy),
        !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
        !is.na(social_class_factor),
        !is.na(compensation),
        !is.na(benefits),
        !is.na(earnings_stability)
      ),
    Hess = TRUE
  ),

  tax_attitudes = MASS::polr(
    ordered(tax_attitudes) ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = gss_attitudes %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(tax_attitudes),
        !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
        !is.na(social_class_factor),
        !is.na(compensation),
        !is.na(benefits),
        !is.na(earnings_stability)
      ),
    Hess = TRUE
  )
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Extract the three JQI component coefficients
# ---------------------------------------------------------

```r
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Extract the three JQI component coefficients
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_coefficients <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  attitude_models,
  names(attitude_models),
  ~ broom::tidy(
      .x,
      conf.int = TRUE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      term %in% c(
        "compensation",
        "benefits",
        "earnings_stability"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      conf.low,
      conf.high
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      outcome = .y
    )
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    component = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      compensation = "Compensation",
      benefits = "Benefits",
      earnings_stability = "Earnings stability"
    ),
    outcome = dplyr::recode(
      outcome,
      redistribution = "Redistribution",
      getting_ahead = "Getting ahead",
      childrens_future = "Children's future",
      political_efficacy = "Political efficacy",
      tax_attitudes = "Tax attitudes"
    )
  )


# Inspect
jqi_coefficients %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    component,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Inspect the coefficients
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_coefficients %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    component,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)



# ============================================================
# 11. EXTRACT JQI COMPONENT COEFFICIENTS
# ============================================================

jqi_coefficients <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  attitude_models,
  names(attitude_models),
  ~ broom::tidy(
      .x,
      conf.int = TRUE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      term %in% c(
        "compensation",
        "benefits",
        "earnings_stability"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      p.value,
      conf.low,
      conf.high
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      outcome = .y
    )
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    component = dplyr::recode(
      term,
      compensation = "Compensation",
      benefits = "Benefits",
      earnings_stability = "Earnings stability"
    ),
    outcome = dplyr::recode(
      outcome,
      redistribution = "Redistribution",
      getting_ahead = "Getting ahead",
      childrens_future = "Children's future",
      political_efficacy = "Political efficacy",
      tax_attitudes = "Tax attitudes"
    )
  )


jqi_coefficients <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  extract_jqi_coefficients(
    model_redistribution,
    "Redistribution"
  ),
  
  extract_jqi_coefficients(
    model_getting_ahead,
    "Getting ahead"
  ),
  
  extract_jqi_coefficients(
    model_childrens_future,
    "Children's future"
  ),
  
  extract_jqi_coefficients(
    model_political_efficacy,
    "Political efficacy"
  ),
  
  extract_jqi_coefficients(
    model_tax_attitudes,
    "Tax attitudes"
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 12. LABEL JQI COMPONENTS
# ============================================================

jqi_coefficients <- jqi_coefficients %>%
  mutate(
    
    component = case_when(
      
      term == "compensation" ~
        "Compensation",
      
      term == "benefits" ~
        "Benefits",
      
      term == "earnings_stability" ~
        "Earnings stability",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    outcome = factor(
      outcome,
      levels = c(
        "Redistribution",
        "Getting ahead",
        "Children's future",
        "Political efficacy",
        "Tax attitudes"
      )
    ),
    
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c(
        "Compensation",
        "Benefits",
        "Earnings stability"
      )
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 13. CHECK THE COEFFICIENTS BEFORE PLOTTING
# ============================================================

jqi_coefficients %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    component,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# ============================================================
# 14. COEFFICIENT PLOT
# ============================================================

jqi_attitude_plot <- ggplot(
  jqi_coefficients,
  aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = outcome,
    shape = component
  )
) +
  
  # Zero line
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  
  # 95% confidence intervals
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      xmin = conf.low,
      xmax = conf.high
    ),
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.55
    ),
    orientation = "y",
    height = 0,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  
  # Point estimates
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.55
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Ordered-logit coefficient",
    y = NULL,
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 16
  ) +
  
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 14
    ),
    
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 13
    ),
    
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 15
    ),
    
    legend.position = "top",
    
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 13
    ),
    
    plot.margin = margin(
      10, 15, 10, 10
    )
  )


jqi_attitude_plot


# ============================================================
# 15. SAVE FIGURE
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "jqi_components_political_attitudes.png"
  ),
  plot = jqi_attitude_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```
